23. **“Akuta ärenden … ingår inte.”** Source: “It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.” “It” denotes the trial note and its reported set. The exclusion remains attached to the reported figures. The substitution of urgent cases for emergencies needs attention; see S2.

24. **“arbeten som beställts före försöket ingår inte”.** Source: “It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.” Same work-order cutoff and exclusion from the reported set. “Beställts” concerns ordering, not completion. No defect.

25. **“Mediantiden från anmälan till tilldelning var två arbetsdagar under försöket, jämfört med tre under de föregående åtta veckorna.”** Source: “Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period.” Same median rather than mean, start and end events, units, values and two eight-week periods. The shared unit “arbetsdagar” also governs “tre”. The report exclusions in the preceding sentence govern the figures. No defect.

26. **“Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna”.** Source: “The periods had different workloads”. Same comparison and qualification, without direction, size or cause added. No defect.

27. **“anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden”.** Source: “the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software.” Same document's assertion and refusal of causal attribution. This does not become a factual assertion that software certainly had no effect. No defect.

28. **“Det finns inga mätningar av kostnader, boendes nöjdhet eller tiden tills reparationerna var klara.”** Source: “There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.” Same three unmeasured outcomes. “Tiden tills reparationerna var klara” means completion time in this reporting context; it does not turn assignment time into completion time or assert that all repairs finished during the trial. No defect.

29. **“Siffrorna ger därför inget svar på dessa frågor.”** Source: “There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.” An authorial inference about these particular numbers' evidentiary limits, with “dessa frågor” referring to those three absent measurements. It does not assert that the outcomes were negative, zero or unknowable from all possible sources. No defect.

30. **Heading: “Maya Lind ser tillbaka på försöket”.** Source: “The trial lasted eight weeks”; “I would choose to do the trial again”; “I would leave an extra week for preparation.” Same speaker reflecting on the completed trial. No unsupported feeling or physical scene. No defect.

31. **Quotation 2: “Vi ägnade mer tid åt att komma överens om kategorierna än åt att registrera de första anmälningarna.”** Source: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports.” Same first-person collective experience and relative time comparison, with no absolute duration manufactured. No defect.

32. **Quotation 2: “Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad börjar använda loggen”.** Source: “I would set that time aside before the next building starts.” The supplied context is a two-building trial of a shared repair log, with preparation for “the next building” and a trial that “has not yet expanded”. The explicit log referent renders the implied start of the next building's participation in the log trial. “Jag skulle” preserves conditional personal advice and does not promise that another building will be added. No defect.

33. **Quotation attribution: “säger Lind i mejlintervjun”.** Source: “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations”; “All interviews occurred by email.” Accurate attribution and medium. “Säger” conventionally reports an email interview response without inventing an oral recording. No defect.

34. **Quotation 3: “Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen.”** Source: “I would choose to do the trial again.” Same first-person conditional choice concerning the trial, not a blanket supplier recommendation. No defect.

35. **Quotation 3: “En samlad vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser.”** Source: “Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.” The present personal assessment stays certain, the preparatory recommendation stays conditional, the reservation remains linked by “men”, and the additional time remains one week. The source further says: “Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures.” The draft respects that distinction. No defect.

36. **“Försöket har ännu inte utökats.”** Source: “The trial has not yet expanded”. Same known lack of expansion, with “ännu” retaining its temporal qualification. No defect.

37. **“Teamet ska fatta beslut efter att ha kontrollerat hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer.”** Source: “the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.” Same decision-maker, future decision, prior check and larger-repair scope. “Ska” preserves warranted future certainty; it does not supply the decision's outcome. No defect.

38. **Heading: “Svale publicerar kundens erfarenheter”; body: “Detta kundcase publiceras av leverantören Svale Systems”.** Source brief: “The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems.” Material: “The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism.” Same publisher and disclosed supplier role. In the publication text, this is supported publication framing, not an invented prior publication event. No defect.

39. **“Som nästa steg kan du läsa [Svales checklista för införande](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist).”** Source: “The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.” Same optional reading action, implementation document and exact URL. “Kan” adds no obligation. No defect.

40. **“bygger på mejlintervjuer och kundens interna försöksanteckning”.** Source: “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations”; “All interviews occurred by email”; “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025”. Same material types and customer ownership of the note. The source itself uses the plural “interviews”; the draft does not specify an unsupported interview count or additional interviewee. No defect.

## Person, number and natural gender

- **“Vi” in quotations 1 and 2; “våra” and “oss” in quotation 1; “oss” in quotation 3:** These convey first-person plural, including the speaker, with no natural-gender specification. Source equivalents are respectively “We”, “ours” and “us”. The maintenance team is the settled contextual collective. Each retains the source's person and number; no claim that every employee or resident participated is added.
- **“Jag” in quotations 2 and 3:** First-person singular, Maya Lind as the speaker; no natural-gender assertion. Corresponding source wording is “I” in each quotation. Same person and number.
- **“dem” in quotation 1:** Third-person plural referring to the categories, matching “them”. It conveys number, not human natural gender.
- **“den tiden”:** The singular demonstrative refers to the category-agreement time just mentioned, matching “that time”. Its grammatical common gender does not identify a person's natural gender.
- **“dess(a)” in “dessa frågor”, and “siffrorna”:** The demonstrative refers to the three outcome questions; plural figures refer to the report count and assignment-time numbers. Neither adds human person or natural gender.
- **“du” in the link invitation:** Second-person singular addressing the article's reader, without natural gender. The supplied brief authorizes an optional reading step for the intended audience. This is address, not an assertion about an identified customer's sex or experience.
- **“företagets eget”, “våra”, “kundens”, “Elm Quays” and “Svales”:** The ownership/association is respectively the company's maintenance team, the speaker's collective's categories, the customer's note, the customer organisation and supplier. “Eget” is grammatical neuter agreement with “team”, not natural gender. Source “its own maintenance team”, “its categories”, “ours” and organisational possessives support those associations.
- **Collective nouns and plural humans:** “teamet” and “personalen” can be grammatically singular while designating multiple people, as can source “team” and “staff”. “Sex medarbetare” retains an explicit count of six. “De boende” corresponds to source plural “residents”. The shifts are collective work groups; the singular names of the shifts do not change their members' number.
- **Maya Lind and the role label:** Source “Her final quotation” explicitly supplies third-person singular feminine natural-gender information. The draft uses the name and “underhållsansvariga”, without a third-person personal pronoun. Swedish definite adjectival “-a” is not, by itself, a uniquely female natural-gender assertion. If the label is read in this named context as female, the source's “Her” supports that reading. The title's occupational scope, independently of gender, is assessed in S1. Nothing in the draft asserts masculine gender, multiple Mayas, or a different speaker.

## Source-support findings

### S1 — Occupational scope in two passages

**Draft:** “underhållsansvariga Maya Lind” in the lead and the introduction to quotation 1.

**Source:** “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind”.

**Difference:** “Supervisor” identifies a supervisory role. “Underhållsansvariga”, read as an occupational title, identifies the person responsible for maintenance. The source provides no statement that Lind holds the customer's general maintenance responsibility; identifying the person does not settle the role's scope. This is an unquoted source-support issue, not a translated-quotation issue and not a gender defect.

**Source true, draft title fails:** Lind could supervise a maintenance shift's staff while a different manager holds the company's maintenance responsibility, budget and overall maintenance decisions. That is compatible with “maintenance supervisor”; the source does not say Lind is the person responsible for maintenance as a whole. The quotation “The maintenance team designed its categories” does not assign that general role to Lind personally. In that case, describing Lind by the broader responsible-person title would misidentify the role.

**Draft title true, source role fails:** A maintenance-responsible technical coordinator could own planning and maintenance decisions while having no staff to supervise; tradespeople might instead report to another manager. Such a person can be “underhållsansvarig” without being a maintenance supervisor. The supplied material has no statement equating these two responsibilities or ruling out that organisational distinction.

**Smallest supported repair:** Use “arbetsledaren för underhåll” in both places: “Här berättar arbetsledaren för underhåll Maya Lind …” and “I en mejlintervju beskriver arbetsledaren för underhåll Maya Lind …”. This preserves the named speaker and supervisory function without adding general responsibility for maintenance.

### S2 — Emergency exclusion broadened to urgent cases

**Draft:** “Akuta ärenden … ingår inte.”

**Source:** “It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.”

**Difference:** The source excludes emergencies. “Akuta ärenden” can include pressing repair cases that are urgent without constituting emergencies. The supplied source does not define its exclusion category as all urgent cases. The difference affects the reported set and consequently the qualifications governing the count and timing figures.

**Draft exclusion true, source exclusion does not establish it:** A repair of a room's nonessential fitting could need prompt handling before a scheduled inspection, making it an urgent case, while posing no immediate hazard and not qualifying as an emergency. Such a report could have been among the trial's 31 reports. Nothing supplied excludes it: “It excludes emergencies” does not exclude all urgent nonemergency work. The draft's broader exclusion would remove that case.

**Source exclusion true, draft exclusion fails:** For an ordinary present emergency requiring immediate response, such as a dangerous active water leak, “akut” also applies; no sound opposite-direction counterexample is established on that ordinary reading. This direction therefore does not independently show a defect. The first-direction counterexample remains: the terms can classify a nonemergency urgent report differently, and no supplied statement equates their extension.

**Smallest supported repair:** “Nödfall och arbeten som beställts före försöket ingår inte.” This preserves the source's emergency category rather than substituting the wider urgency category. Keep the pre-trial work exclusion intact.

## Separate translated-quotation assessment

**Quotation 1:** Source: “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.” Draft: “Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen.” The ordinary first-person voice, past desire, already-completed work, customer ownership and supplier's assisting role remain. The Swedish is idiomatic. No concrete obstruction to the same meaning or distinctive voice; no translation finding.

**Quotation 2:** Source: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.” Draft: “Vi ägnade mer tid åt att komma överens om kategorierna än åt att registrera de första anmälningarna. Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad börjar använda loggen”. The comparative experience remains separate from the conditional personal advice. “Avsätta” idiomatically renders reserving time. The surrounding source settles the otherwise compressed “building starts” as the next building's participation in the log trial; making the log explicit does not invent a scheduled expansion. No concrete obstruction to meaning or voice; no translation finding.

Teamet valde Svale Systems efter att ha testat om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation. Underlaget innehåller ingen jämförelse med någon annan leverantör.
